name: Goleuddydd

attributes.attribute: Welsh princess whose name means bright day and who hid an ancient fertility goddess
wife of Prince Cilydd who could not conceive and feared a barren throne
bore her son Kulhwch in a swineherd's sty after raging through the wilderness
son of Goleuddydd whose name means pig
similar disguised form of an ancient pig goddess of fertility

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Goleuddydd is a Welsh heroine or goddess. Her name means bright day. This ancient fertility goddess, read into her legend, is rooted in Celtic or pre-Celtic belief. She married Prince Cilydd but could not conceive. Her people feared a barren throne without an heir. When she finally became pregnant she went mad. She refused to live indoors and raged through the wilderness. That motif also appears in the Irish tale of Mess Buachalla. She bore her son in a swineherd's sty and named him Kulhwch, meaning pig. Like Rhiannon, she hides an ancient pig goddess of fertility.

okr.objective: Frame Goleuddydd as a Welsh princess whose story veils an ancient fertility goddess.
